title: Setting Up TensorFlow 🛠️
description: Install TensorFlow and verify your environment.

slides.title: Installation Made Easy 📥
slides.content:
# Get TensorFlow Running

The easiest way is via **pip**, Python’s package manager.

Open your terminal and type:
```bash
pip install tensorflow
```

That’s it! For GPU support, use `tensorflow-gpu` (though recent versions auto‑detect).

* 🐍 Requires Python 3.7–3.11
* 💻 Works on Windows, macOS, Linux
* 📦 Can also use `conda install tensorflow`

slides.title: Virtual Environments 🛡️
slides.content:
## Keep It Clean

Always create a dedicated environment to avoid dependency conflicts:

```bash
python -m venv tf_env
source tf_env/bin/activate   # macOS/Linux
tf_env\Scripts\activate      # Windows
pip install tensorflow
```

slides.title: Verify Installation 🧪
slides.content: Run this script to confirm TensorFlow works and see what devices you have:
slides.codeSnippet:
import tensorflow as tf
print("Version:", tf.__version__)
print("GPUs Available:", tf.config.list_physical_devices('GPU'))

slides.title: GPU? 🚄
slides.content: If you have an NVIDIA GPU, install the **CUDA** and **cuDNN** libraries to speed up training by 10x or more. The TensorFlow website has a step‑by‑step guide.
